questions.q: Which vector database is fully managed only, with no self-hosted or open-source option?
options: Qdrant
Weaviate
Pinecone
Milvus
questions.explain: Pinecone is a fully managed, serverless service — there's no version of it you install and run yourself, unlike Qdrant, Weaviate, and Milvus, which are all open-source.

questions.q: What does it mean that Chroma runs "embedded" by default?
options: It runs inside your own application process, with no separate database server to stand up
It requires a dedicated GPU server to operate
It only works inside a web browser
It can only store a fixed, small number of vectors
questions.explain: Embedded means the database runs in-process alongside your own code, which is what makes Chroma the fastest option to start prototyping with locally — no server to install or connect to.

questions.q: What does the category a vector database falls into (managed, self-hosted, or embedded) actually tell you?
options: How many programming languages it supports
Whether it can store text at all
Which one produces the mathematically most accurate similarity search results
What you're signing up to operate, not which one has inherently "better" search quality
questions.explain: The core operations — create, upsert, query, delete — are the same across all of them; the category is about operational responsibility, not search quality.

questions.q: In the Qdrant Cloud cluster overview screenshot shown in this lesson, what does the tabbed layout (Overview, API Keys, Metrics, Logs, Backups, Configuration) represent?
options: The kind of operational screen a vendor's managed console gives you so you don't have to run that infrastructure yourself
A code editor for writing SQL queries
A billing invoice for the account
A list of every vector stored in the collection
questions.explain: This is what "fully managed" looks like in practice — metrics, logs, and backups are handled through the console instead of infrastructure you'd have to set up and maintain yourself.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what determines the right vector database to start with for a given RAG pipeline?
options: Always whichever one is newest on the market
There is one single correct choice for every project
Scale, ops budget, and whether you already need features like hybrid search or heavy metadata filtering on day one
Only the number of GitHub stars the project has
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that none of this is a permanent ranking — the right pick depends on your project's scale, how much infrastructure you want to operate, and which features you need immediately.
